Package com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules

Class LinkValidationRule

java.lang.Object
com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules.LinkValidationRule
All Implemented Interfaces:
AuditRule
public final class LinkValidationRule extends Object implements AuditRule
AuditRule that validates all anchor links found on a rendered HTML page.

Checks performed

  1. Broken links – HTTP HEAD request per unique href; any response outside 2xx or 3xx, or a connection failure, is a finding.
  2. HTTP (non-HTTPS) links – any href using the plain http:// scheme flags a security/mixed-content concern.
  3. Missing unsubscribe link – no anchor whose href or visible text matches recognised unsubscribe patterns (CAN-SPAM / GDPR compliance).
  4. Unresolved merge/template tags – any href still containing a literal, unpopulated template placeholder (e.g. href="{{ADV_UNSUB_LINK}}"). See "What changed and why" below.

What changed and why

An href left as an unresolved merge tag — e.g. href="{{ADV_UNSUB_LINK}}" — previously slipped past every existing check:

  • checkUnsubscribePresence(java.util.List<com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules.LinkValidationRule.LinkEntry>, java.util.List<java.lang.String>, java.util.List<java.lang.String>) matches on the anchor's href or visible text against an unsubscribe-like pattern. An anchor with text "Unsubscribe" and href="{{ADV_UNSUB_LINK}}" matches on text alone and was reported as a present, valid unsubscribe link — the href's actual content was never inspected.
  • checkBrokenLinks(java.util.List<com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules.LinkValidationRule.LinkEntry>, java.util.List<java.lang.String>, java.util.List<java.lang.String>) only probes hrefs that literally start with http:// or https://. A merge tag like {{ADV_UNSUB_LINK}} doesn't start with either, so it was silently skipped by the broken-link prober entirely — never reported as broken, because it was simply never checked.

The net effect: an unpopulated merge tag on a legally-required unsubscribe link could pass this rule cleanly with no finding at all. checkUnresolvedMergeTags(java.util.List<com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules.LinkValidationRule.LinkEntry>, java.util.List<java.lang.String>) closes that gap directly — it scans every anchor's raw href (regardless of scheme, and independently of anchor text) for the literal {{...}} placeholder syntax and fails immediately on a match, before any HTTP probing is attempted.

Findings format

Every broken hyperlink produces an individual structured finding via FindingFormatter.brokenLink(String, String, String), e.g.:

 Broken Link
   Displayed Text  : Download Report
   Destination     : https://example.com/report
   Validation      : FAILED
   Reason          : HTTP 404 Not Found

Multiple broken links are never aggregated into one string.

PASS evidence

When the rule passes, it now also returns evidence findings via RuleResult.Builder.withFindings(List) so the dashboard can show exactly what was checked, not just that nothing failed:

  • one finding confirming the unsubscribe link was found,
  • one finding per successfully probed HTTP/HTTPS link, e.g.: 
           Broken Link
         Displayed Text  : Download Report
         Destination     : https://example.com/report
         Validation      : PASSED
         Reason          : HTTP 200 OK
    (the same title is reused for symmetry with the FAIL case — only the Validation/Reason fields differ).

No insecure-link evidence is produced on PASS, since an empty insecure-link set means there was nothing to probe — there is no individual link to point to. Likewise, no unresolved-merge-tag evidence is produced on PASS, for the same reason.

Link extraction

All <a href="…"> elements are collected via a Playwright evaluate() call, which returns resolved absolute URLs exactly as the browser would compute them.

Broken-link probing

HTTP probing is done with HttpURLConnection HEAD requests in a fixed-size thread pool. Each probe has an independent connect/read timeout; failures are recorded per URL without aborting the rest of the batch.

Thread safety

All Pattern instances and configuration constants are static final. An ExecutorService is created and shut down within each execute(Page) call — no shared mutable state escapes the method. The class is safe for concurrent use from multiple TestNG threads.
